_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for ONGC, standalone (domestic E&P), Rs crore. One segment ('ep') whose revenue and EBITDA come from the price x volume and cost build in 'build' (checked in tools/authoring/ONGC.ctx.js). ONGC is valued as the street values it: a sum of the parts of the standalone business on P/E (core profit, before dividends from the stakes), the listed stakes at the 30-Sep-2026 closes less a holding discount, ONGC Videsh and the unlisted subsidiaries. Parts are written by tools/authoring/ONGC.val.js.

segments.name: ONGC standalone (domestic E&P)
segments._why: Growth and margin are copied from the build below by ONGC.val.js (see 'build'). FY26 revenue Rs132,506 cr (crude 63%, gas 27%, value-added products 9%); EBITDA margin 46.6% after exploration write-offs. Q1FY27: revenue +45% to Rs46,460 cr, margin 61% at US$99.45/bbl.

_unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in the segment
_unallocWhy: Single business: all costs are in the segment.

build._baseWhy: FY26 actuals (AR FY26 ten-year table): crude Rs83,810 cr on 18.79 MMT sold, gas Rs36,330 cr on 15.491 BCM; Brent US$70.45 (AR MD&A), INR/US$ 88.31 (PPAC). Gas US$7.3/mmBtu = average 'overall' realisation of the FY26 quarters (JM: US$7.1-7.6). Each line scales with volume, price and the rupee.
build._crudeVolWhy: Q1FY27 crude production -5% YoY (KG-98/2 reservoir problems, Western Offshore pipeline work, well shut-ins during project hook-ups); management expects oil to recover to about last year's level by year-end and +~0.5 MMT in FY28 (half of the ~1 MMTOE FY28 gain). PL cut FY27E standalone oil to 18.9 MMT production (-2%).
build._brentWhy: FY27E: Q1 ~US$97.5 (management), Jul-Sep ~US$96, then the EIA Sep-2026 path (US$90 in 2H2026, ~US$85 in Q1-2027). FY28E: EIA's US$77 in Q2-2027 and ~US$67 in 2H2027 and after. FY29E: US$70, between EIA's 2027 exit and management's US$75+ long-run view. The street uses US$80 FY27E and US$70-75 from FY28E. Realisation tracks Brent (contracts with refiners at a small premium; Q1FY27 US.45 vs Brent ~US-98).
build._fxWhy: Rupee ~95.4/US$ in Aug-2026 (JM key data) vs 88.31 FY26 average; we assume ~1.5% a year depreciation thereafter.
build._gasVolWhy: Q1FY27 gas sales 3.7 BCM (-4% YoY; offtake problems at isolated fields). New gas from DUDP (+2 mmscmd by Dec-26), East Coast CPP (1.3), Tapti/Daman (0.5) and KG-98/2 (3 mmscmd by Q4FY27, 6-7 by Q4FY28): management guides +1 BCM in FY27 production and ~+0.5 MMTOE gas in FY28. PL: FY28E gas production 20.4 BCM (+5%).
build._gasPriceWhy: Q1FY27 US$9.2 overall (APM capped at US$7.00, new-well gas US$13.31 on 24% of sales). FY27E: formula price US$9.0 in Sep-2026 falls with crude, so new-well gas (1.2x the formula, uncapped) eases to ~US$10-11: US$8.7 average. FY28-29E: at ~US$70 crude the formula (10% of the Indian basket) is ~US$7.0, at or below the US$7.25-7.50 ceiling; new-well gas ~US$8.4 on 28-30% of volumes: ~US$7.8 overall.
build._vapWhy: LPG, naphtha, ethane-propane: FY26 Rs11,879 cr; Q1FY27 ~Rs3,830 cr (JM) at US$97 crude. Scaled with crude and the rupee.
build._cessWhy: OIDB cess (charged on nomination crude) = 15.55% of crude revenue in FY26 (Rs13,034 cr).
build._royaltyWhy: Royalty was 10.8% of crude and gas revenue in FY26 (Rs12,965 cr). Cut from 8-May-2026: offshore crude 9.09%->8%, gas 10%->8% (onland nomination crude restored to 16.66% on 4-Jun-2026): about -1.1 point on the FY27 mix, for ~10.5 months of FY27.
build._leviesWhy: National calamity duty ~Rs86 cr; no windfall tax (SAED abolished Dec-2024, not re-imposed by 30-Sep-2026; bear case adds it back).
build._opexWhy: FY26 Rs28,209 cr (+2.7%). Q1FY27 ~Rs6,500 cr. +5% in FY27E (rupee weakness lifts dollar-linked rig and vessel costs), +4.5% a year after.
build._explWhy: Survey plus dry wells: FY25 Rs9,826 cr, FY26 Rs9,729 cr (Q4FY26 dry wells Rs5,110 cr). Q1FY27 low (dry wells Rs1,108 cr; surveys delayed by retendering) but management expects a big post-monsoon survey programme and more deepwater wells (Rs800-1,000 cr each) under Samudra Manthan.
build._otherWhy: Provisions and write-offs (FY26 Rs3,948 cr) plus exchange loss (Rs2,699 cr) and other items: Rs6,702 cr in FY26. Q1FY27 implies ~Rs1,100 cr a quarter; the rupee's fall keeps FY27 high.

_capexWhy: Guidance US$3.5-4.0 bn a year (Rs33,000-38,000 cr at Rs95); FY26 Rs35,878 cr. The engine adds capex to the gross block and the cost build already expenses dry wells, so we enter capex less ~Rs8,500-10,000 cr of exploratory wells that end up written off: Rs35,000 / 36,500 / 37,500 cr of total spend.
_depWhy: Depletion, depreciation and amortisation (incl. impairment) Rs25,134 cr in FY26; Q1FY27 Rs6,283 cr (Rs25,100 cr a year). Rate set so FY27E is ~Rs25,500 cr.
_treasuryWhy: Other income is built (below), not a yield on 'treasury', because the engine's treasury here also holds the stakes at book value.
_otherIncomeWhy: FY26 Rs10,356 cr = interest Rs4,051 cr (bank deposits Rs2,174 cr on Rs28,660 cr cash; site-restoration fund Rs1,617 cr) + dividends Rs4,807 cr (HPCL 1,811, IOC+GAIL 2,202, MRPL 502, Petronet 188, OVL 51, PMHB 53) + other Rs1,498 cr. TTM Jun-26 Rs11,007 cr; Q1FY27 Rs1,861 cr (no dividends in Q1). FY27E: interest 4,100 + dividends 4,000 (HPCL's Q1 loss rules out interims) + other 1,500; FY28E 4,300 + 4,200 + 1,500; FY29E 4,500 + 4,500 + 1,500.
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs4,529 cr, Q1FY27 Rs1,086 cr: mostly interest on Rs25,822 cr of lease liabilities (rigs, vessels); borrowings only Rs7,823 cr.
_taxWhy: Statutory 25.17%; dividends received are deductible under section 80M, so the effective rate is ~25.17% x (PBT - dividends) / PBT. Set by ONGC.val.js from the build.
_payoutWhy: FY26 DPS Rs13.25 (interims Rs6.00 and Rs6.25 plus a final) = 51% of EPS (Rs16,669 cr); FY24-25 38-43%. With FY27E profit ~75% higher we assume a 40% payout (MOSL 38%): DPS rises, the ratio falls.

dcf._betaWhy: A commodity producer with state ownership: market-like sensitivity; cost of equity 12.5%. Debt is small (borrowings Rs7,823 cr), so the cost of equity is used as the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Mature, depleting fields: 1% nominal terminal growth (house range 5-6% is for growing businesses). ONGC 1P reserves (518 MMtoe) are ~13 years of FY26 output; it holds production flat only with continuous capex, so we fade growth to 1%.
dcf._fadeWhy: Margin fades to 45% (FY26 47% at US crude, before any windfall tax); capex to 20% of revenue (FY24-26 ~25% incl. written-off wells); depreciation 17% of revenue (FY26 19%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Brent stays near US$80 after the Hormuz premium (management's US$75+ view); KG-98/2 and the Western Offshore projects lift output ~4% a year; no windfall tax; the market keeps a 20% holding discount and values OVL at MOSL's ₹23 a share.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Brent falls to ~US$60 as EIA's 2H2027 surplus deepens, or a windfall tax returns; output stays flat; HPCL's losses deepen and the holding discount widens to 25% (MOSL, PL); OVL at JM's ₹7 a share; OPaL worth nothing.

parts.name: ONGC standalone (core): P/E on Sep-28E core profit
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E core profit (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E, before dividends from the stakes) ₹37,610 cr × 3.5x (bull 5.5x on ₹47,076 cr, bear 2.5x on ₹26,922 cr)
parts.note: ONGC's own implied forward P/E on core profit since Apr-2021 (median 3.3x), times the +2.2% oil-and-gas sector move at 30-Sep-2026.

parts.name: MRPL: 71.63% stake at market
parts.note: Subsidiary (HPCL holds a further 16.96%); AR FY26 note 11.1.

parts.name: Less: holding discount on the listed stakes
parts.metricLabel: Base 20%, bull 20%, bear 25% of the listed stakes
parts.note: House rule for listed stakes inside an operating company: 20% unless the street clearly differs (JM and BOB 20%, MOSL and PL 25%, Geojit 50%).

parts.name: ONGC Videsh (100%)
parts.metricLabel: ₹15 a share: midpoint of JM (7x FY28E EPS, ₹7) and MOSL (0.5x FY25 book, ₹23); bull MOSL, bear JM
parts.note: Overseas E&P; Sakhalin-1 restored from Jan-2026; ONGC cost ₹15,000 cr.

parts.name: Other unlisted subsidiaries, JVs and associates at cost
parts.metricLabel: OPaL ₹21,181 cr, ONGC Green ₹4,700 cr, others ₹1,711 cr (bear: OPaL at zero)

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values ONGC (JM, MOSL, PL, Geojit): standalone on P/E plus the stakes.

methods.name: P/E on standalone EPS
methods.why: ONGC's own one-year-forward P/E on reported standalone EPS since Apr-2021: median 5.5x (no trough years in the window), times the 2.2% sector move: 5.5x. It prices the stakes through their dividends, at ONGC's multiple.

methods.name: DCF (standalone, plus investments at book)
methods.why: Standalone free cash flow; the engine's net cash includes ONGC's investments at book value (cost for subsidiaries, fair value for IOC and GAIL).
